title: Global Temperature Change Analysis
text:
Introduction
This project analyzes global temperature change across three climate periods, beginning with the 1961–1990 WMO Climatological Reference Period and extending through the 2021–2025 Recent Climate Interval, using data from the NASA Goddard Institute for Space Studies (GISS).
The analysis examines temperature change from several complementary perspectives, including long-term temporal trends, statistical distributions, hemispheric differences, latitude zones, seasonal patterns, surface-area distributions, and global spatial patterns.

title: Global Temperature Change Analysis
text:
Temperature Anomalies
Temperature change is expressed using temperature anomalies rather than absolute temperatures. An anomaly represents the difference between an observed temperature and a reference-period average.
The NASA GISTEMP data used in this project express temperature anomalies relative to the 1951–1980 baseline. This reference baseline is retained throughout the analysis so that all reported anomaly values have a consistent interpretation.

title: Global Temperature Change Analysis
text:
Climate Periods
The project uses three non-overlapping analysis periods and one consistent terminology throughout the workflow:

WMO Climatological Reference Normals (1961–1990) — the 1961–1990 period retained by WMO as a standard reference period for long-term climate-change assessment.
WMO Climatological Standard Normals (1991–2020) — the current WMO 30-year climatological standard normal.
Recent Climate Interval (2021–2025) — a project-defined recent five-year interval used to identify emerging climate signals. It is not a WMO climatological normal.

For compact tables or figures, the project uses the abbreviations REF, CSN, and RCI. These labels are intended to be used consistently in this project and in the companion Global Climate Classification Change Analysis project.

title: Global Temperature Change Analysis
text:
Workflow
The analysis is organized as a reproducible workflow consisting of three stages:

Data Acquisition
Download the latest NASA GISTEMP temperature data and Natural Earth coastline data, and document the project software environment and acquired datasets.
Data Transformation
Clean, transform, aggregate, and spatially prepare the source data; calculate grid-cell areas; and save reusable transformed datasets.
Data Visualization
Create statistical summaries and visualizations examining global time series, climate-period distributions, hemispheres, latitude zones, seasons, surface-area distributions, and global gridded temperature patterns.

title: Global Temperature Change Analysis
text:
Data
Temperature data are obtained from the NASA GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP) project.
The source data used in this analysis include:

Global monthly temperature anomalies
Northern Hemisphere monthly temperature anomalies
Southern Hemisphere monthly temperature anomalies
Latitude-zone annual temperature anomalies
Global gridded monthly temperature anomalies in NetCDF format

The global coastline is obtained from Natural Earth and is used as a geographic reference layer for the global maps.

title: Global Temperature Change Analysis
text:
Software
Programming Language: R
Development Environment: Positron
Document Creation: Quarto
R Packages:

gt – summary tables
fs - files
ncdf4 – NetCDF processing
pals – diverging color palettes
patchwork – plot layouts
rnaturalearth – geographic coastline data
R.utils – gzip decompression
sf – spatial data processing
tidyverse – data manipulation and visualization
viridisLite – sequential color palettes

Exact software and package versions used for the project are documented in the Data Acquisition chapter.

title: Data Acquisition
text:
Download Temperature Anomalies


Show code
for (i in seq_len(nrow(file_catalog))) {

  if (file_catalog$format[[i]] == "CSV") {

    filename <- file_catalog$filename[[i]]
    source_url <- file_catalog$source_url[[i]]

    download_path <- paste0(
      source_url,
      filename
    )

    latest_path <- path(dir_raw, filename)
    archive_path <- path(dir_archive, filename)

    download.file(
      url = download_path,
      destfile = latest_path,
      mode = "wb",
      quiet = TRUE
    )

    file_copy(
      path = latest_path,
      new_path = archive_path,
      overwrite = TRUE
    )

    message(
      "Updated: ",
      filename
    )
  }
}




Show code
for (i in seq_len(nrow(file_catalog))) {
  if (file_catalog$format[[i]] == "NetCDF") {
    filename <- file_catalog$filename[[i]]
    source_url <- file_catalog$source_url[[i]]
    download_path <- paste0(
      source_url,
      filename,
      ".gz"
    )

    latest_path <- path(dir_raw, filename)
    archive_path <- path(dir_archive, paste0(filename,".gz"))

    temporary_path <- paste0(
      archive_path,
      ".download"
    )
    download.file(
      url = download_path,
      destfile = temporary_path,
      mode = "wb",
      quiet = FALSE
    )
    file_move(
      path = temporary_path,
      new_path = archive_path
    )
    R.utils::gunzip(
      filename = archive_path,
      destname = latest_path,
      overwrite = TRUE,
      remove = FALSE
    )
  }
}

title: Data Transformation
text:
Initialization
Objective: Transform the acquired temperature anomaly data into analysis-ready datasets for evaluating global temperature change. This notebook standardizes the NASA GISTEMP data, assigns observations to the REF, CSN, and RCI climate periods, derives temporal and spatial summaries, and saves the transformed datasets used for visualization.
Show code
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(gt)
  library(fs)
  library(ncdf4)
  library(sf) 
})
Show code
dir_raw <- path("data", "raw")
dir_transformed <- path("data", "transformed")

file_name_nc <- "gistemp1200_GHCNv4_ERSSTv5.nc"
netcdf_path <- path(dir_raw, file_name_nc)

source("R/climate-periods.R")

analysis_start_year <- min(climate_periods$start_year)
analysis_end_year <- max(climate_periods$end_year)

mollweide_crs <- "+proj=moll +lon_0=0 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +datum=WGS84 +units=m"

geographic_id_levels <- c("G", "S", "N")

zone_levels <- c(
  "90S-24S", "24S-24N", "24N-90N",
  "90S-64S", "64S-44S", "44S-24S", "24S-EQU",
  "EQU-24N", "24N-44N", "44N-64N", "64N-90N"
)

climate_period_levels <- climate_periods$period_abbr
Show code
assign_climate_period <- function(year) {
  cut(
    year,
    breaks = c(
      climate_periods$start_year,
      analysis_end_year + 1
    ),
    labels = climate_periods$period_abbr,
    right = FALSE,
    ordered_result = TRUE
  )
}

Transformation Summary

transformed_descriptions <- tribble(
  ~filename,                     ~dataset,
  "monthly.rds",                 "Monthly temperature anomalies",
  "annual.rds",                  "Annual temperature anomalies",
  "decade.rds",                  "Decadal temperature anomalies",
  "seasonal.rds",                "Seasonal temperature anomalies",
  "hemisphere.rds",              "Hemisphere anomalies by climate period",
  "zone.rds",                    "Latitude-zone anomalies by climate period",
  "gridded.rds",                 "Gridded anomalies by climate period"
)

transformed_catalog <- tibble(
  path = dir_ls(
    dir_transformed,
    type = "file"
  )
)

file_metadata <- file_info(transformed_catalog$path)

transformed_catalog <- transformed_catalog |>
  mutate(
    filename = path_file(path),
    format = path_ext(filename),
    directory = path_dir(path),
    transformation_datetime = format(
      file_metadata$modification_time,
      "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"
    ),
    file_size_kb = round(
      as.numeric(file_metadata$size) / 1024,
      0
    )
  ) |>
  left_join(
    transformed_descriptions,
    by = "filename"
  ) |>
  arrange(filename) |>
  select(
    dataset,
    filename,
    format,
    directory,
    transformation_datetime,
    file_size_kb
  )

title: Data Visualization
text:
Initialization
Objective: Visualize the transformed temperature anomaly data to examine how global temperature change varies over time, across climate periods, and by geographic and seasonal characteristics. This notebook summarizes temporal trends, temperature distributions, hemispheric and latitude-zone differences, seasonal patterns, affected surface area, and concludes with global maps comparing the REF, CSN, and RCI climate periods.
Show code
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(gt)
  library(fs)
  library(patchwork) 
  library(pals) 
  library(viridisLite) 
  library(sf)
})
Show code
build_maps <- TRUE

dir_raw <- path("data", "raw")
dir_transformed <- path("data", "transformed")

source("R/climate-periods.R")

theme_climate <- theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 6)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 16, margin = margin(b = 10)),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12, color = "black"),
    axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 0.5, color = "black"),
    axis.ticks.length = grid::unit(4, "pt"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.key.width = unit(1.2, "cm"),
    legend.key.height = unit(0.5, "cm"),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

legend_climate <- guide_colorbar(
  direction = "horizontal",
  title.position = "top",
  title.hjust = 0.5,
  barwidth = unit(10, "cm"),
  barheight = unit(0.45, "cm"),
  ticks = TRUE
)

# Diverging temperature-anomaly palette
anomaly_colors <- pals::coolwarm(11)

# Sequential climate-period palette
climate_period_palette <- setNames(
  viridisLite::viridis(
    nrow(climate_periods),
    option = "D",
    begin = 0.25,
    end = 0.80
  ),
  climate_periods$period_abbr
)

# Categorical hemisphere palette
hemisphere_palette <- c(
  "N" = viridis(5)[2],
  "S" = viridis(5)[4]
)

# Categorical season palette
season_palette <- c(
  "Winter" = "#0072B2", # blue
  "Spring" = "#009E73", # bluish green
  "Summer" = "#E69F00", # orange
  "Autumn" = "#CC79A7" # reddish purple
)

anomaly_fill_scale <- function(limits) {
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = anomaly_colors[1],
    mid = anomaly_colors[6],
    high = anomaly_colors[11],
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = limits,
    name = "Anomaly (°C)",
    guide = legend_climate
  )
}

Area
Surface-area distributions quantify how much of the observed global grid experiences temperature anomalies at or above different thresholds.


Show code
weighted_quantile <- function(x, w, probs) {
  keep <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(w)
  x <- x[keep]
  w <- w[keep]
  ord <- order(x)
  x <- x[ord]
  w <- w[ord]
  cumulative_weight <- cumsum(w) / sum(w)
  sapply(
    probs,
    function(p) {
      x[which(cumulative_weight >= p)[1]]
    }
  )
}

          area_km2[avg_anomaly > 0],
          na.rm = TRUE
        ) /
        sum(
          area_km2[!is.na(avg_anomaly)],
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
    pct_area_above_1 =
      100 *
        sum(
          area_km2[avg_anomaly > 1],
          na.rm = TRUE
        ) /
        sum(
          area_km2[!is.na(avg_anomaly)],
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

v7_statistics_table <- v7_statistics |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -climate_period,
    names_to = "statistic",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    statistic = recode(

    ),
    climate_period =
      climate_period_labels[as.character(climate_period)]
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = climate_period,
    values_from = value
  )
